title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 15-18). Grothendieck is setting up an 'algebra of figures' on an underlying object L. In the image L is written as a script L, which the transcription renders inconsistently as \mathcal{L} or \mathcal{F}. The ingredients are: an ordered set F (or \mathfrak{F}) of 'figures' or 'stables' A, which are subsets of L; a sub-figure order; sups of families; and for each A a 'multistable' structure F_A (a multiplicity), from which an interior A^0 = A \ \partial A is defined. On p.16 he notes that this data recovers only the Stone completion of L. He then reformulates it with a Stone (compact, totally disconnected) space X and clopen families, and identifies support/cosupport pairs with pairs of regular open sets (U = int cl U, V = ext U).

This page, dated 15 June, makes a general remark about restricting the class of admissible figures:

1. F may be replaced by various ordered subsets Phi of F that are stable under taking sub-figures (lying in F) and under sup. Such a Phi is a hereditary, sup-closed subclass, an 'ideal' of figures.

2. Examples when L is a (Hausdorff) topological space:
   - require the A to be closed, or compact, or closed and connected;
   - more generally, any condition on the A as subsets of L, or as multistables, or on the multistables F_A, is said to define such a sub-ordered set;
   - conditions on the interior A^0, whose definition depends on the multiplicity F_A: A^0 connected, or more generally i-connected for 0 <= i <= infinity;
   - conditions on the boundary: \partial A a topological sphere, so the figures are 'cells'.

3. If L is 'modérée' (tame, in the sense of Esquisse d'un programme §5), one restricts to Phi ⊂ P(L) consisting of tame subsets. One can also impose more global conditions on Phi.

4. The page continues on p.18 with an example of a global condition: local finiteness, which gives stability under finite sups only. It then defines finite figures and figures of finite type (contained in a finite union of sub-figures F_A). Finally it treats a stratification of a triangulable space X by closed cells X_x indexed by a poset L, with A -> X_A = ∪_{x∈A} X_x giving a bijection between downward-closed ('admissible') subsets of L and closed unions of strata.

5. Left-margin addition, partly illegible. It apparently says one should also demand a compatibility of the multiplicities F_A with inclusion, namely monotonicity of interiors: A ⊂ B ⇒ A^0 ⊂ B^0.

What this serves: classifying admissible 'figure' classes so that combinatorial data (posets of strata, cells) and geometric data (tame or cellular subsets of a space) match. This is the bridge, completed on p.18, between face posets with their Alexandrov topology and cellular or tame stratified spaces.
errors: The blanket claim that 'any condition' on the A, or on the F_A, defines an ordered subset with the required stabilities (under sub-figure and under sup) is false as stated. Connectedness, 'closed and connected', i-connectedness of A^0, and '\partial A is a sphere' are not inherited by sub-figures in general. Compactness and closedness are not preserved under infinite sups. Grothendieck partly corrects this on the next page: local finiteness gives stability only under finite sups, not arbitrary ones.

The margin's monotonicity requirement A ⊂ B ⇒ A^0 ⊂ B^0 is a genuine extra axiom. It fails for the naive manifold-interior: an arc inside a disc has nonempty interior as a 1-manifold, but it does not lie in the disc's interior when it meets the boundary. So the dependence of A^0 on F_A is essential, and the condition is not automatic.

ideas.what: Restricting the lattice of figures to hereditary, sup-closed subclasses defined by topological conditions (closed, compact, connected).
ideas.modern_name: Ideals / hereditary subfamilies in a lattice of subsets; ideals of subcomplexes

ideas.what: Figures whose interiors are i-connected (0<=i<=infinity) and whose boundaries are topological spheres, i.e. cells; interior depending on an extra 'multiplicity' structure.
ideas.modern_name: Regular cell complexes / regular CW complexes; cells with prescribed connectivity
ideas.usually_credited_to: J.H.C. Whitehead; regular CW complexes, Björner (1984) for face posets
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 discusses tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures, though not in this formulation

ideas.what: Restriction to tame ('modérée') subsets when L is tame.
Global conditions on the class of figures, such as local finiteness, giving closure only under finite sups (continued on p.18).
ideas.modern_name: Locally finite families / locally finite CW complexes

ideas.what: Monotonicity axiom for interiors: A ⊂ B ⇒ A^0 ⊂ B^0, depending on the multiplicity data.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of relative interiors with the face order (as in polyhedral or regular cell complexes, where it is not literally true for faces)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatics of 'figures' as subsets carrying a multiplicity (multistable) structure, with an intrinsic interior A^0 = A \ ∂A. He proposes classes of figures cut out by connectivity of A^0 and sphericity of ∂A, in a tame setting. This amounts to a program of axiomatising regular-cell or tame-cell structures via a lattice of figures, linking a combinatorial poset with its Alexandrov topology to tame stratified spaces. It is not developed in the literature under his name; related modern work (face posets of regular CW complexes, exit-path / stratified homotopy theory, o-minimal cell decomposition) arose independently.
missed.quote: Ou on peut demander aux ∂A d'être des sphères topologiques etc. Si 𝓛 est modérée, on se bornera aux Φ ⊂ 𝔓(𝓛) pour lesquels A ∈ Φ ⇒ A partie modérée de 𝓛
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest: it documents how Grothendieck intended to make the Esquisse's 'topologie modérée' concrete through a combinatorial 'algebra of figures'. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary and partly imprecise.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine remarks on restricting a class of figures by topological conditions (closed, compact, connected, cells, tame). Its general stability claim is overstated. The only mildly notable points are the explicit link to tame topology and cellular conditions inside the unpublished 'Algèbre des figures', and the margin's monotonicity-of-interiors axiom. Neither is a new result.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, the underlying object is written as a script 𝓛 in the image; the transcription alternates between \mathcal{L} and \mathcal{F}.
Line 3: the insertion above 'sous-figure' reads roughly '(qui finissent dans F)' or '(qui sont dans F)'. The struck words are 'par ∩ et par sup' (or similar) before 'sous-figure'.
Line 4: 'Si 𝓛 est un espace topologique' has '(séparé)' or a similar word inserted, apparently 'séparé'.
Line 12: 'Signalons, ici, une propriété(s)' — this most likely introduces properties of A^0 = A \ ∂A, i.e. 'des propriétés portant sur A^0'. The 'NB' insertion is uncertain.
Line 17: 'Si 𝓛 est [inserted word, possibly 'variété'] modérée'. The word 'modérée' is underlined, and an insertion above it is not captured in the transcription.
Bottom margin formula reads approximately 'A ≤ B^0 i.e. A⊂B ⇒ A^0⊂B^0'. The rest of the margin is barely legible: 'Mais il serait raisonnable de demander ... F_A ... Aussi, la condition d'être ...'.
